summary: Anthropic alleged in June 2026 that operators affiliated with Alibaba’s Qwen lab used large numbers of fraudulent accounts to query Claude for capability extraction. Its September threat report expanded the claimed campaign to more than 151 million May–July exchanges, described a fixed prompt designed to elicit Opus reasoning traces, two account pools, saved transcripts and use in Qwen training; it said it banned one pool and the traffic shifted. These are detailed first-party findings and attribution claims, not independently audited account logs or a judgment against Alibaba. The report’s separate sensitive-user-data examples concern other labs, not the Alibaba campaign. The precise economic loss, any user-data exposure in this bounded campaign and Alibaba’s response remain unresolved.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Anthropic reports account-route evasion, extraction of reasoning traces and use of those outputs in Qwen training by Alibaba-linked operators. The campaign crossed required access routes and appropriated restricted capability value; its continuation despite account enforcement supports the campaign-level control-effect finding. Activation of a particular response-level anti-distillation control remains unresolved. The cumulative acquisition for downstream model training is independently supported as the reported extraction mechanism. Attribution, telemetry and ultimate lineage remain provider-bounded and have not been independently verified.

The first account-pool ban did not contain the campaign, which shifted traffic to a second pool; campaign-specific effectiveness of anti-distillation controls remains unresolved.

assessment_boundaries: Anthropic is an interested provider and its raw account telemetry is unavailable; Alibaba-linked attribution is not an adjudicated finding.
The June 28.8m and later May–July 151m figures overlap and are not additive.
Other labs’ rerouted customer data in the same report must not be transposed to Alibaba.
Use of distillation as a technique can be legitimate; the alleged fraud, access restrictions and missing secondary-purpose authority are the disputed governance features.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters reported Anthropic’s June allegation. Anthropic’s original Senate letter claimed 28.8 million exchanges via nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts from 22 April to 5 June. Its September threat report describes a larger May–July set of more than 151 million attributed exchanges, a fixed prompt eliciting reasoning traces from Opus 4.6/4.7, saving them as supervised fine-tuning material and using them in Qwen models; it describes almost 5,000 accounts in an initial obfuscated pool and a shift after bans. These figures cover different observation windows and should not be added. The provider can report its own observed traffic and bans, but the attribution to Alibaba, ultimate training lineage and legal status are not independently verified here. The same report’s sensitive data relaying examples are explicitly Moonshot, DeepSeek or Xiaomi, not evidence of an Alibaba privacy incident. No quantified commercial damage, operational cost or resulting model uplift attributable to these exchanges is established.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Anthropic’s September report supplies detailed first-party telemetry and attribution, but remains a provider account rather than an independently audited dataset or adjudication against Alibaba. Its facts support distinct account-routing, extraction, and model-training components. The anti-distillation control’s campaign-specific activation state is not described, so control effectiveness remains unresolved. The report’s separate examples of sensitive user-data relaying concern other labs and are not part of this Alibaba case. First-party attribution supports the preserved routing and capability-value findings within its stated scope. The activated account ban’s inadequate campaign effect remains distinct from an unspecified anti-distillation control’s unresolved state. The reported campaign-level account-control effect is Not aligned. The provider’s tracing of the campaign is Aligned for inquiry support. Other security processes and receiving-model training-data verification remain Boundary where their decisive records are not available. Sensitive-user-data examples from other labs remain outside this case.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case illustrates the difference between allowed model consultation, bulk capability extraction and account-eligibility evasion. Later provider detail supports more than a generic allegation but is still not independent proof of the named actor. The report cannot supply a privacy harm in this particular campaign merely because other campaigns in the same document relayed sensitive user data.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Primary and first-hand reporting reconstructed as material external action, risk/control effect and response episodes; provider assertions and observation scope are distinguished rather than mechanically asserted as independently proven.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic attributed a May–July 2026 high-volume Claude extraction campaign to operators linked to Alibaba/Qwen. It reported two fraudulent-account pools, residential proxy routes, disposable account details and virtual-card payment methods; the first large pool was banned but traffic was promptly shifted to a second pool. The attribution and estimated more than 151 million exchanges are Anthropic's investigative findings, not a judicial determination.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A service’s account eligibility and access restrictions should remain effective across linked account pools and proxy routes; reaching the service through a technically available API or account does not establish eligible authority.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic reports fraudulent account pools and proxy routes that obfuscated access and allowed continued traffic after the first pool was banned, indicating the required account-eligibility route was avoided.
The reported ban was operative for the first pool, but the campaign promptly shifted to a second pool; the effect did not contain the attributed activity at campaign level.
The provider describes coordinated, persistent acquisition through distributed fraudulent account pools and proxies under an adverse access basis; the downstream training purpose is preserved inE003.

clauses.source_paraphrase: In the reported campaign, fixed prompting elicited additional reasoning-like material from Opus outputs. Anthropic described anti-distillation protections generally, but did not document a particular control's trigger, activation and expected effect for each extracted response. Whether an activated response-level control had inadequate effect therefore remains unresolved.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A reasoning-protection control should produce its required protective effect on the extraction request; the particular control’s applicability and activation in this campaign must be established before judging effectiveness.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Existing anti-distillation measures and successful extraction are reported, but the report does not establish which specific control became operative for these responses. Successful extraction alone cannot establish that an activated control's protective effect was inadequate.

The report does not identify the required trigger of a particular applicable control or show that the control failed to activate. Continued extraction may raise a question about protective effect, but it cannot substitute for evidence of that activation state.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic states that the generated reasoning transcripts were saved and turned into supervised fine-tuning data for Qwen model development and related research. The provider links the captured data to training and capability development but does not disclose complete dataset lineages or an independent audit of the accused organisation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reasoning outputs generated in response to service queries should not be treated as unrestricted inputs to a separate model-training and capability-development program without an independently adequate basis.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The provider attributes large-scale use of its reasoning traces to another lab’s model training and R&D, describing material capture of value dependent on its capability without an adequate basis.

The report describes covert extraction through fraudulent access. It does not show valid permission for an original data-processing purpose being treated as authority for a secondary purpose. The supported mechanism is instead appropriation of restricted model capability value through the reported campaign.

The provider reports captured reasoning incorporated into Qwen training, completing the independently evidenced cumulative capability-acquisition purpose; campaign scale and adverse authority are preserved inE001.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic detected the alleged campaigns, banned related accounts and strengthened controls; its own description makes clear that removing the first fraudulent-account pool did not terminate traffic when the operation shifted to a second pool. Later disruption statements must be read alongside that contemporaneous containment shortfall, not as proof that every request was blocked.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Response effectiveness should be assessed against the continuing campaign across related access routes, rather than treating action on one pool as complete containment.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The first account ban did not contain the campaign, although subsequent detection, disruption and safeguard changes are reported as response measures.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: Working HIM 1.1.0 minimum-data-access calibration: S2 Privacy & Confidentiality recognises Anthropic's first-party report of actual unauthorised harvesting and retention of non-public model reasoning transcripts in the Alibaba/Qwen campaign. This does not assert customer personal-data disclosure, a verified number of successful transcripts, independent proof of recipient-model training or statutory wrongdoing. Anthropic attributes the activity to Alibaba, but that attribution and all downstream model-training effects remain provider findings, not independently adjudicated facts. The campaign's substantial scale and claimed training use warrant separate S3–S5 upper-severity review; upper severity remains unresolved; 151 million exchanges are attempts/traffic, not measured successful protected reasoning records. Other eleven dimensions retain their evidence-limited statuses. S2 is a minimum established level under the current working criterion, not a finding that the overall event was minor.

Minimum supported S2 confidentiality harm: Anthropic's 10 September 2026 originating provider investigation expressly reports that Claude Opus 4.6/4.7 protected chain-of-thought reasoning traces were elicited, saved as transcripts and used for model training within the attributed Alibaba/Qwen extraction campaign. The claimed extraction of otherwise non-public protected model reasoning is a materialised confidential-information access event under the revised working HIM 1.1.0 privacy S2 criterion; it is not merely attempted probing or a hypothetical future data leak. This is evidence of Anthropic's own systems and its first-party account, not independent verification of Alibaba attribution, training lineage or total successful output count. The reported 151 million exchanges are not 151 million confirmed protected-reasoning disclosures or injured individuals. User personal-data examples attributed to other labs do not belong to this case. Higher privacy, financial, operational, intellectual-property or reputational impact remains unresolved; S2 is a supported minimum, not a ceiling.

Retain unresolved SU while preserving provider-reported transcript harvesting and downstream training use. Campaign-scale capability acquisition independently meets the industrial-extraction class, not a quantified harm threshold. Request/account counts are not unique harmed people. Sensitive-customer-data examples belong to other named campaigns. Actual low/remediable economic disruption and material bounded organisational loss were tested separately; the public account does not establish those consequences to Anthropic, so no financial band is invented or withdrawn.

aggregate_harm_screening.rationale: Anthropic's Claude Opus models were deployed through accessible services when misuse occurred. However, the observed bounded consequence is unauthorised harvesting of Anthropic's protected reasoning; this is a specific institutional confidentiality case, not an evaluation of a feature-wide collective harm mechanism within the five eligible Aggregate Harm domains. The exclusive specific_consequence route is retained.
